title: heterogeneous-quantized-capacity-profiling-and-slo-contract-2026
author: Marcus Li
content:
Overview

Purpose: This runbook defines a standard process for profiling capacity and establishing SLO-backed capacity contracts for heterogeneous model fleets that include quantized variants (FP16, INT8, 4-bit). It codifies a repeatable measurement matrix, acceptance thresholds, a handoff contract between Models and SRE, and an operational escalation path when actual traffic violates the contract.

Scope: inference-runtime services (GPU and accelerator-backed pools), capacity-orchestrator, slo-telemetry pipeline, and warm-pool management. Applies to hosted and Dedicated customers; procedures for Private deployments are included with notes on network/airgap constraints.

Why this matters
- Quantized variants reduce token cost but change latency profiles, memory footprint, and tail behavior.
- Heterogeneous deployments (mix of quantized and full-precision models) require explicit headroom to preserve SLOs during traffic shifts and tail bursts.
- A standardized SLO contract reduces ambiguous ownership when model rollout changes capacity needs.

Key definitions
- SLO consumer: team owning product SLAs (e.g., chat-service).
- Model steward: team owning model variants and prompting.
- Capacity owner: SRE team that manages capacity-orchestrator configuration for a tenant.
- Contracted capacity: baseline GPU / accelerator allocation reserved for a tenant or workload.

Service-level targets (examples to adapt per product tier)
- Latency-critical generation: p50 < 60 ms, p95 < 160 ms, p99 < 280 ms (seq_len 128, non-streaming).
- Standard generation: p50 < 120 ms, p95 < 300 ms, p99 < 800 ms (seq_len 256).
- Embeddings/Indexing: p50 < 40 ms, p95 < 120 ms.
- Throughput availability: 99.9% of tokens processed within SLO window (monthly).
- Error budget: 0.1% monthly for latency breaches for latency-critical tier.

Profiling matrix (must be collected for every model variant prior to admission)
- Dimensions collected: model_name, model_variant, quantization (FP16/INT8/4-bit), sequence_length, batch_size, continuous_batching_on (true/false), KV_cache_enabled (true/false), p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), tokens_per_second, gpu_mem_gb, gpu_util_pct, inference_threads, observed_tail_outliers_per_10k, warm_pool_reserve (instances).

Example profiling table (text table representation)
| model_name | variant | quant | seq_len | batch | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | tps | gpu_mem(GB) | gpu% | warm_pool |
| llama-7b | baseline | FP16 | 128 | 1 | 52 | 138 | 250 | 48 | 14 | 72 | 4 |
| llama-7b | quant-v1 | INT8 | 128 | 1 | 60 | 150 | 330 | 62 | 9 | 65 | 6 |
| codex-lite | quant-low | 4-bit | 64 | 2 | 38 | 110 | 260 | 96 | 6 | 58 | 8 |

Minimum profiling procedure (9 steps)
1) Reproduce representative traffic: use production prompt/sequence samples (at least 10k unique requests) and the same token distribution used by the customer.
2) Run cold-start baseline: measure p50/p95/p99 for single-instance cold (empty KV cache). Record memory and load times.
3) Run warmed baseline: prepopulate KV cache for representative sessions and spin warm pool to target size; measure latencies.
4) Sweep batch sizes 1,2,4,8 and continuous batching enabled/disabled; capture throughput vs latency curves.
5) Measure quantized variants with identical prompts; run multiple trials at different concurrency levels to capture tail behavior.
6) Record GPU perf counters (utilization, SM/PCIe stalls), host-side metrics (CPU steal, NIC drops), and platform scheduling latencies.
7) Run stress sweep for tail: inject bursts at +3x expected 1-minute peak to capture degradation modes.
8) Collect traces and spans via slo-telemetry and attach to profiling artifact. Include raw sample IDs for reproducibility.
9) Produce artifact: CSV + JSON summary, attached to model onboarding ticket and archived to /data/profiles/<model>/<variant>/<date>.

Acceptance criteria for admission to hosted/dedicated pools
- For the target customer tier, p99 must be <= contracted SLO p99 in warmed baseline with warm_pool_reserve accounted for.
- Throughput at contracted concurrency must meet tokens_per_second target with GPU_util_pct <= 85% (buffer for scheduling spikes).
- Memory footprint must leave >= 10% free GPU memory to allow for kernel scratch and dynamic batch growth.
- Observed_tail_outliers_per_10k less than 25 for latency-critical tier.

SLO-backed capacity contract template (YAML snippet)
- tenant: "acme-chat"
- model_set:
  - name: "llama-7b"
    variant: "quant-v1"
- contracted_capacity:
  gpu_count: "8"
  warm_pool_instances: "6"
  headroom_pct: "20"
- slo_targets:
  latency_p99_ms: "280"
  availability_pct: "99.9"
- autoscale_policy: "hybrid-reserve"
- monitoring:
  slo_alert_channel: "#slo-acme-chat"
  telemetry_stream: "slo-telemetry.acme-chat"

Operational checklist for onboarding (owner: Model steward + Capacity owner)
- [ ] Profiling artifact uploaded and linked to ticket.
- [ ] Contract YAML reviewed and signed by SRE and Product (slo sign-off).
- [ ] Capacity-orchestrator reservation created (gpu pool + warm pool).
- [ ] Canary traffic plan defined (traffic %, duration).
- [ ] Trace sampling and synthetic canaries configured on slo-telemetry.
- [ ] Rollout playbook scheduled (canary -> gradual -> full) with rollback triggers.

Canary rollout procedure (recommended)
1. Configure canary in capacity-orchestrator with 5% traffic for 60 minutes.
2. Monitor slo-telemetry for p95/p99 and tail sample traces; check error budget consumption ledger.
3. If p99 exceeds contracted by >10% for 5 continuous minutes, pause rollout and run rollback.
4. If resource usage (gpu_util_pct) exceeds 90% persistently, increase contracted_capacity or reduce concurrency.
5. After 24 hours of stable canary (no SLO breaches and <10% error budget consumption), increment to 25% for 2 hours, then 50% for 4 hours, then full.

Alerting and escalation rules (oncall actions)
- Severity P1: sustained p99 > contracted_p99 + 20% for >10 continuous minutes OR error budget burn rate > 3x.
  - Action: page primary SRE oncall, page model steward, instantiate emergency capacity buffer (hot-add 20% reserved if available).
- Severity P2: sudden increase in tail outliers (>100 per 10k) or gpu OOM events.
  - Action: run diagnostics playbook, enable degraded routing to fallback model variant, open incident ticket.

Fallback strategies (priority)
1) Route to compatible lower-cost variant with stricter token limits (e.g., quant-v2 with smaller seq_len).
2) Enable prefix caching for deterministic prompts where applicable.
3) Temporarily limit tenant concurrency via token-priority capacity gate.
4) Burst to a geographically different region with spare capacity (follow data residency constraints).

Runbook: immediate triage checklist (oncall)
1) Validate telemetry: confirm p95/p99 and token processing counts in slo-telemetry.
2) Check capacity-orchestrator: active GPUs, queue lengths, warm_pool health.
3) Inspect recent deployments: model steward deploys in last 30 minutes (release metadata).
4) If OOMs or kernel failures: reduce concurrency and migrate some traffic to fallback variants.
5) If scheduling/backpressure: escalate to Capacity owner for emergency scale.
6) Record all actions to incident ticket and attach profiling artifacts.

Post-incident requirements
- Incident review must include: profiling artifacts (pre/post), sample traces, evidence of contract violation, root cause hypothesis, remediation plan, and a capacity remediation ticket.
- If a model rollout caused the incident, revert to a previous variant and require a re-profile with extended stress tests before re-admission.
- Update SLO contract if model behavior differs materially (>=25% change in tokens_per_second or p99).

Tooling commands and example snippets
- Profile run (CLI):
  rwinfer profile --model llama-7b --variant quant-v1 --batch-sizes 1,2,4 --seq-lens 32,128,256 --concurrency 1,5,10 --out /tmp/profiles/llama-7b-quantv1.csv

- Create capacity reservation (example curl to internal API):
  curl -X POST https://capacity-orch.internal/api/v1/reservations \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"tenant":"acme-chat","gpu_count":8,"warm_pool":6,"headroom_pct":20}'

- Sample slo-telemetry query (pseudo):
  SELECT quantile(0.99, latency_ms) AS p99, count(*) AS samples FROM slo_telemetry
    WHERE tenant='acme-chat' AND model='llama-7b' AND variant='quant-v1' AND ts > NOW() - INTERVAL '15 minutes'

Governance and periodic review
- Quarterly review: every model contract is reviewed by SRE and Model steward. Review includes fresh profiling at current production distributions, headroom re-evaluation, and a decision to change contracted_capacity.
- Pre-deprecation: models scheduled for deprecation must publish a migration plan that maintains SLOs for dependent tenants.

Owner & contacts

- Model steward contact: models-team@redwood.com
- Capacity-orchestrator owner: infra-gpu-team@redwood.com

Appendix: common failure modes and mitigations
- Kernel inefficiency for 4-bit paths: mitigation: pin to FP16 or alternate INT8 variant for latency-critical traffic until kernel patches are live.
- Scheduling jitter due to autoscaler churn: mitigation: increase warm_pool_reserve and adjust autoscale cooldown to 90s.
- KV cache thrashing under multi-tenant prefix patterns: mitigation: per-tenant prefix caching limits and prioritized cache retention for latency-critical tenants.

Artifact locations
- Profiles: s3://redwood-inference/profiles/<model>/<variant>/<date>/profile.csv
- Contract records: vault://slo-contracts/<tenant>/<contract-id>.yaml
- Incident tickets: Jira project RWINF-SRE (link included in incident review template).

Notes and references
- See runtime-architecture page for kernel selection logic.
- See slo-telemetry spec for required labelled spans and sampling rules.
- This document is intended to be updated as quantization kernels and scheduler heuristics evolve.

End of document.
